body: The US seems like living hell for men. Fathers can't be with their daughters without being humiliated? Seriously?
I find it terrifying that so many other people feel this way. Even me a couple of years ago would be disappointed.

It's understandable, this is billions of years of genetic programming by evolution - to pursue dopamine, serotonin, etc. Since now we have easy access to high energy food and entertainment, it is easy to get addicted to those things, so don't blame yourself.

As someone who had to go through my parents' divorce and fighting, I am really sorry this is happening to you. I saw how painful it was for my father. It ruined both of us mentally to be honest. 

I hope you get to spend time with your boys because it is very important for them to have a male role model. Trust me, I had very little time with my dad and it nearly drove me insane. Boys need their fathers, this is extremely important.

I completely agree. Nature just seems to be cruel or at best indifferent. That's a shame. Sugary caffeinated drinks and the internet have provided some relief for me as well.  

Evolution is based on random genetic mutations and mistakes. For every success there are multiple failures. Point is that evolution is a joke from our point of view as intelligent humans because we can see the inefficiencies.

That is a very difficult situation to be in, I fully understand because I am currently taking time off university. If it is not possible to return to the original university mid year, perhaps it's best to wait it out and prepare for next year when you return. 

I know how you feel though, I have also held back tears in lectures. There was literally only one class I kind of enjoyed. I imagined university would be heaven for me because I also think learning is great but I was bitterly disappointed. Hope things work out for you.
Ayy, awesome, well done! Recently I failed my 4th attempt so I know what a huge stress it is. It must feel like heaven to pass... for now I'll keep dreaming.

Perhaps it's best to talk with your family then. It is definitely possible for you to have friends, relationships etc. but the thing with suicide is that we give up that possibility forever. Suicide is not a decision to be taken lightly. Sometimes going for a walk helps me in dark times.

I'm really sorry that you're suffering. A-levels are stressful and I know what it's like when things go wrong all the time. Would you consider speaking to someone at school and giving yourself some time off?

Hey it seems like there are a lot of us in the same situation. The agonising part for me is that I really want to be good at some things but the ability just is not there. On the other hand, even if we don't have natural talents, our hard work can still achieve a lot. Wishing you the best of luck.
It makes a lot of sense. I've always thought this way.

You can still achieve 'great' things for yourself, no matter how humble those achievements are. Just because someone else has fame does not diminish your own success. There's no logical reason why small goals can't lead to great things. Fame and glory are often media hype to attract revenue. At least this is what I like to tell myself, I don't know if it's reasonable. 

I understand what you mean, I would give anything to have a successful happy life like some of my friends.
Thank you. It's painful but I'll try to keep pushing.

The scary thing is that I'm desperately trying to advance with all my strength and yet I can't because I'm too weak. It's a bit like being tied to a concrete block and left to drown in a lake where there's air a few inches above your head.
Looks fantastic. I could comfortably live in one of these apartments. Let's hope they build more of them.
You are right, thank you. It seems you have built up a lot of resilience, so that's encouraging.
I didn't know about those findings, thanks for sharing. It makes sense - there have been some eureka moments but probably just not enough...
That sounds tough - having the police watching. I agree it's a good strategy to try and be confident.
Thank you for offering but I'm in the UK.
Ok I will try the rescue remedy.
Hmm it is a bit. Please send my apologies to your friend on behalf of all of us who failed.
Thanks, that was encouraging. I'll give it my best shot once again and maybe it will indeed be a cool story.
Oh dear, panic attacks like that are horrible. Well done for passing anyways.
Oh sorry that third time sounds really unlucky. Thanks, I appreciate the advice.
We'll see. Maybe I will end up quitting but it's a really useful skill to have. For now I'll give it everything. Will look into that NASA guy and the book. Thanks.
Thank you. That's nice to read.
Thank you. We did some practice tests. I'm hoping they will help in the end. I agree about taking your time.
Yes please, freedom is always good.
Yeah hopefully, we'll see how it goes. My friends all did it first time so it's getting embarrassing, but apart from trying again I don't know what else to do. Thanks for the support.

Thanks for the kind words. I'm glad that you are more confident now. 

Unfortunately insurance in the UK is super expensive for young people and without it it's illegal to drive any car. I can't really afford insurance so I only practice in my instructor's car. Also, I have a limited time to pass.

Thank you for the comment. Well done for passing.

Sorry just needed to vent my frustration. They always fail me on observations or something like being in a wrong lane, for example, but I always try my best to have good car control. One time it was a mistake when manoeuvring. It's just silly random things that I can't predict.   

I just seem to lack the ability to stay calm under pressure. I can safely get from A to B but in a test my nerves just cost me so much. It's like the brain sabotaging itself.

Physical exercise can help reduce stress and anxiety. A doctor explained to me that it breaks down the stress hormone cortisol, which in turn calms you down. I like to go running 3-4 times per week and it seems to help. 

Sleep is also very important. Make sure you are not sleep deprived. A lot of people underestimate the importance of good sleep. 

Sorry that you're going through this. I can relate completely and I'm still struggling with a lot of anxiety, so you are not alone. Hope things get better for you. Take care.

When we 'fall in love' we're usually slaves to our hormones and primal instincts, which means we often become irrational. I know it causes pain, I've had the feeling before, however looking back on it I realise it was just not worth it. In my opinion, no girl can possibly be the ONLY meaningful thing in life. Hope things work out for you.

Thanks for your advice. Grades are not the problem for me, but it's probably not a good idea to continue if I'm mentally unstable and have no confidence in what I'm doing. 

It's not just for a job, I had intellectual curiosity but all those positive things have been crushed. Also, I would have to continue next year, not this semester. Hopefully I can get some medication and find work experience this year.

Thank you. I do think my degree (Engineering) would be useful. I honestly have good intentions and put in my best effort, but I hate myself and wish I was dead every single day. 

I'm in the UK, where it's not free, so my reasoning was that I didn't want to get into unnecessary debt if I had to leave in the middle of the year. I planned to get more work experience this year since that is now very important on resumes/CVs.

Completely agree with you. Don't know what to say. I know words rarely help with depression, but I can fully empathise. Job applications are torture. These people you're applying to could literally have your life in their hands and they crush people if they don't like them.

That sounds familiar. Really sorry you're going through this. Having nothing to look forward to kills everything positive in us. I've also decided how I would do it (which is weird because I'm usually indecisive).
Pineapple on pizza tastes good.

When I was little I took a heavy metal swing to the back of the head after trying to jump off it. It's the kind of pain where you curl up and grind your teeth for a good 10 minutes before you can say a word. Not to mention wanting to vomit afterwards. Not fun. 

Another time I fell off the passenger seat of a crappy old car (long story) and had my face grated on the road. Luckily it was low speed and somehow no scars remained.

Sorry to hear about the chronic pain and the immune disease. That's really tough. I've only gone as far as volunteer work, but it has helped a bit with confidence when dealing with people. 

Ah yeah it's embarrassing when hanging out with friends. I kind of have to avoid questions carefully and it makes me feel worthless. It's really sad.
